detail.extracted_title: Musandam Winter Season Launches with 75 Cultural and Coastal Adventure Events
detail.excerpt: Under the theme "Musandam: An Experience to Live," the northern governorate opens six months of fjord sailing, mountain trails, heritage carnivals, and community markets
detail.article_html:
Where towering limestone cliffs plunge straight into the emerald currents of the Strait of Hormuz, northern Oman is preparing for its most ambitious winter tourism calendar to date. Under the patronage of His Highness Sayyid Bilarab bin Haitham Al Said, Minister of State and Governor of Muscat, and in the presence of Sayyid Ibrahim bin Said Al Busaidi, Governor of Musandam, the promotional ceremony in Muscat officially launched the 2026–2027 "Musandam Winter" season under the banner "Musandam: An Experience to Live."

Spanning 75 cultural, sporting, entertainment, and marine events across the governorate's wilayats and coastal villages, the winter program positions Musandam as a premier cool-season destination for regional and international travelers. Designed around the governorate's dramatic fjord geography and maritime traditions, the season pairs outdoor adventure with direct economic opportunities for local small and medium enterprises, productive families, and traditional artisans.

Festivals From Khor Sham to Kumzar and Lima

The 2026–2027 calendar anchors each area of the peninsula with signature community gatherings that celebrate Musandam's coastal identity. Flagship events include the Musandam Carnival, the Strait of Hormuz Festival, and Musandam Cultural Days, which bring folk arts, maritime storytelling, and regional cuisine to the waterfront.

In the northernmost maritime settlements, the Kumzar Festival spotlights the unique linguistic and seafaring customs of one of Oman's most iconic coastal communities, while the Lima Bazaar creates an open-air marketplace for traditional weavers, potters, and culinary entrepreneurs in the seaside village of Lima. Further south along the western coast, the Bukha Lights Festival illuminates historic fortifications and shorelines with evening installations, complemented by a Kite Festival, a Community Sports Championship, motorsports rallies, and equestrian competitions.

Fjord Sailing, Freediving, and Mountain Ziplines

Beyond its scheduled festivals, the Musandam Winter season highlights the peninsula's year-round natural amphitheater for outdoor exploration. Visitors can board traditional wooden dhows to sail through the sheltered sea inlets and towering rock corridors of Khor Sham, where resident pods of Indo-Pacific humpback and bottlenose dolphins swim alongside wooden hulls.

For adventure travelers, the program integrates high-altitude and deep-water itineraries across the governorate. Over the past two years, Musandam has expanded its adventure infrastructure—anchored by the record-breaking mountain zipline in Khasab overlooking the fjords—alongside marked mountain trekking trails leading to ancient stone villages, coastal kayaking routes, cliffside camping sites, padel courts, and guided scuba diving and freediving excursions across coral reefs teeming with pelagic marine life.

Decentralizing Tourism Value Under Oman Vision 2040

Speaking at the launch ceremony, officials emphasized that the winter season reflects Oman Vision 2040's focus on governorate-led economic decentralization. Rather than concentrating tourism infrastructure in a single hub, the 75-event calendar distributes visitor footfall across Khasab, Bukha, Dibba, Madha, Lima, and Kumzar.

By connecting local boat operators, mountain guides, homestay hosts, and craftspeople directly with seasonal visitors, the Musandam Winter program turns natural topography into sustainable household income—inviting travelers to experience the quiet majesty of Oman's northern fjords alongside the people who have navigated these waters for generations.

  • Oman Daily
detail.instagram_caption:
Northern Oman's dramatic fjord peninsula has officially launched its 2026-2027 "Musandam Winter" season under the theme "Musandam: An Experience to Live." Patronized in Muscat by His Highness Sayyid Bilarab bin Haitham Al Said alongside Sayyid Ibrahim bin Said Al Busaidi, Governor of Musandam, the program brings 75 cultural, marine, and adventure events across the governorate.

From the sheltered turquoise inlets of Khor Sham to the coastal villages of Kumzar and Lima, this season connects outdoor adventure with community entrepreneurship:

- Signature Cultural Gatherings: Flagship programs include the Strait of Hormuz Festival, Musandam Carnival, Musandam Cultural Days, the Kumzar Festival, the Bukha Lights Festival, and the open-air Lima Bazaar supporting local artisans and productive families.
- Marine & Fjord Expeditions: Traditional dhow sailing through the towering limestone corridors of Khor Sham, dolphin watching, coastal kayaking, scuba diving, and freediving across living northern coral reefs.
- Mountain Adventure & Sports: High-altitude ziplining in Khasab, guided mountain village treks, cliffside camping, equestrian championships, kite festivals, and motorsports rallies.

Explore the full guide to the Musandam Winter 2026-2027 season at omanspire.om (link in bio).

seo_metadata.featured_image_alt_text: Minimalist Swiss serigraph editorial illustration of Musandam limestone fjord cliffs, a traditional Omani dhow, leaping dolphins, and Omani observers on a cliff terrace.
seo_metadata.visual_prompt: Minimalist mid-century Swiss serigraph and lineless faceted geometric editorial illustration celebrating the Musandam Winter Season and coastal fjord adventures in northern Oman. Monumental, surreal conceptual composition where towering origami-faceted limestone cliffs of the Khor Sham fjords in warm desert sand ochre and burnt terracotta plunge into deep midnight navy and electric marine teal waters, with a geometric traditional Omani wooden dhow silhouette gliding across angular diagonal light reflections and two minimalist geometric dolphin silhouettes arcing through the water under dramatic diagonal chiaroscuro shadow planes. In small environmental scale, minimalist faceless geometric silhouettes of an Omani man in a crisp off-white dishdasha and embroidered kumma cap and an Omani woman in a modest flowing black abaya and shayla headscarf standing on a high faceted cliffside stone terrace overlooking the serene marine strait. Strictly lineless flat color planes with zero black comic outlines, zero facial features, zero floating arrows or glowing tablets, and subtle screenprint risograph paper grain texture. Curated high-contrast palette of deep midnight navy shadows, warm desert sand ochre, burnt terracotta coral, clean cream off-white, and a focused accent of marine teal. High-end New Yorker, Economist, and Monocle magazine cover art aesthetic. Strictly no realism, no text, no words, no letters, no typography, no labels, no signs, no numbers baked into the artwork, strictly no frame, no border, no white margin, no matting, seamless full bleed composition extending to all four edges.
